why: A proves Lemma 2.4 only for M = E, a complete normed space (any dimension, where the infinite-dimensional case is degenerate: X = 0). B states it for an abstract finite-dimensional Hausdorff manifold. B ⇒ A: specialize M := E, translate the tangent-bundle section to ContDiff, and translate 'generates' (B tests against all smooth g; A uses HasDerivAt) using dual functionals. The infinite-dimensional case is handled separately by Riesz's theorem (X = 0, so the flow is id). A ⇒ B would need global flows on an arbitrary manifold (patching local flows with charts), which is genuinely missing from A.
